If not, use the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / 2a. The discriminant (b² - 4ac) tells you the number of real solutions. If it's positive, two solutions. If zero, one. If negative, no real solutions.

To find the stationary points, take the derivative of f(x), call it f'(x). Then solve f'(x) = 0. The solutions are the x-values of the stationary points. Plug these values back into the original equation to find the corresponding y-values. You can then classify each point as a maximum, minimum, or point of inflection depending on the second derivative.
